_what: CC-LEARNING-ENGINE-L0 acceptance 3 — reference outputs from a published FSRS-4.5 implementation.
_why_this_version: v2.1.0 is FSRS-4.5, which is what D3 pins. Verified from its own source rather than its version number: src/fsrs/fsrs.py has DECAY = -0.5 and FACTOR = 0.9**(1/DECAY) - 1 (= 19/81), the power forgetting curve (1 + FACTOR*t/S)**DECAY, the LINEAR initial difficulty w4 - w5*(r-3), and a 17-value parameter vector. FSRS-4 used an exponential curve and FSRS-5 uses 19 parameters and an exponential D0 -- neither matches. fsrs-rs v1.3.1 was checked first and rejected: it already ships 19 parameters, so it is FSRS-5.
_why_their_weights_and_not_ours: These are the weights that test hardcodes, NOT the FSRS-4.5 defaults and NOT ours. That is the point. Running our formulas on their parameters tests the ARITHMETIC; running ours on ours would only re-assert our own constants. Our pinned FSRS_W is checked separately against the published 4.5 default set.
_reading_the_history: Thirteen reviews, thirteen intervals, but only TEN are memory-state outputs. py-fsrs runs a card through New -> Learning -> Review -> Relearning, and the three zeros are same-day scheduler steps that do not touch S or D: review 1 (New, memory initialised but the card is held in Learning), and reviews 8 and 9 (Relearning steps). The remaining ten are the core trajectory this fixture tests.
_interval_equals_stability: At the 0.9 target retention FSRS's interval reduces to round(S): interval = S/FACTOR * (0.9^(1/DECAY) - 1), and FACTOR is defined as exactly that same quantity, so the two cancel. The published interval list is therefore a published STABILITY trajectory, rounded, which is what makes it usable as a core vector at all.
